## Installation

```{r cran-installation, eval = FALSE}
# Install release version from CRAN
install.packages("descriptr")

# Install development version from GitHub
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("rsquaredacademy/descriptr")

# Install the development version from `rsquaredacademy` universe
install.packages("descriptr", repos = "https://rsquaredacademy.r-universe.dev")
```

## Usage

We will use the `wholesale_customers` data set in the below examples. It
contains annual spending by 440 wholesale customers on six product categories,
together with the sales channel and region of each customer. The data come from
the UCI Machine Learning Repository (Cardoso 2013, CC BY 4.0).

```{r load, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
library(descriptr)
```

```{r egdata}
str(wholesale_customers)
```

### Continuous Data

#### Summary Statistics

Annual spending on fresh products averages 12000.30, with a median of 8504 and
a standard deviation of 12647.33. The distribution is right-skewed.

```{r descript1}
ds_summary_stats(wholesale_customers, fresh)
```

#### Frequency Distribution

With four intervals, 400 of the 440 customers (90.91%) spend less than 28040 on
fresh products.

```{r descript4}
ds_freq_table(wholesale_customers, fresh, 4)
```

### Categorical Data

#### One Way Table

Most customers are in the hotel/restaurant/cafe channel: 298 (67.73%) against
142 (32.27%) in retail.

```{r descript3}
ds_freq_table(wholesale_customers, channel)
```

#### Two Way Table

Customers in both channels are concentrated in the other region: 70.81% of
hotel/restaurant/cafe customers and 73.94% of retail customers.

```{r descript2}
ds_cross_table(wholesale_customers, channel, region)
```

### Group Summary

Grouping by channel shows that hotel/restaurant/cafe customers spend more on
fresh products on average (13475.56) than retail customers (8904.32).

```{r descript5}
ds_group_summary(wholesale_customers, channel, fresh)
```

#### Multiple Variable Statistics

```{r descriptr6}
ds_tidy_stats(wholesale_customers, fresh, milk, grocery)
```

## Features

- Summary statistics
- Two way tables
- One way table
- Group wise summary
- Multiple variable statistics
- Multiple one way tables
- Multiple two way tables
